fatal_errors: The proposed solution is an unspecified thermal-sprayed coating rather than bulk ZrB2–30% AlFeNiCoCr cermet parts consolidated by spark plasma sintering.
It omits the key composition, the 1500 °C optimum, and the densification/binder-overflow dependence on sintering temperature.
The cited evidence does not demonstrate resistance of the proposed coating to molten aluminum; it only provides general statements about high-temperature or wear properties of high-entropy alloys.
No specific coating chemistry is given, so the claimed chemical inertness toward molten aluminum is not testable as a materials-selection claim.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the general need to reduce molten-aluminum corrosion and proposes a barrier mechanism, but it does not reconstruct the target material or processing route. The target is a ZrB2 cermet containing 30% equimolar AlFeNiCoCr binder, optimized by SPS at 1500 °C. Its performance follows from high density and uniform binder-mediated grain bonding; processing at 1600 °C causes binder loss and renewed porosity. The generated answer instead proposes a generic thermal-sprayed coating, compares it only with an uncoated substrate, and supplies no molten-Al exposure temperature or duration. Its control experiment could test a specified coating, but as written it cannot discriminate among compositions or establish the claimed chemical inertness. The references concern general HEA oxidation, wear, and high-temperature behavior and do not validate thermal-spray integrity or corrosion resistance in molten aluminum.
